title: Goldilocks and the Three Bears
author: Traditional
source: Public domain. Retold from the traditional English tale.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Once upon a time there were three bears who lived in a cozy house in the woods: great big Papa Bear, middle-sized Mama Bear, and wee little Baby Bear. One morning, Mama Bear cooked porridge for breakfast, but it was too hot to eat.

segments.speaker: mama-bear
segments.text: "Let us walk in the woods while it cools,"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: she said. And off they went.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Just then, a little girl called Goldilocks came wandering by. She peeped in at the window, and then at the keyhole, and when she saw nobody was home, she opened the door and walked right in. On the table sat three bowls of porridge.

segments.speaker: goldilocks
segments.text: "Oh, I am SO hungry!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: First she tasted the porridge in the great big bowl.

segments.speaker: goldilocks
segments.text: "Ouch! Too hot!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then she tasted the porridge in the middle-sized bowl.

segments.speaker: goldilocks
segments.text: "Brrr! Too cold!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then she tasted the porridge in the wee little bowl, and it was just right — so she ate it all up.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Feeling full, Goldilocks went to sit down. The great big chair was too hard. The middle-sized chair was too soft. But the wee little chair was just right — until CRACK! It broke all to pieces beneath her.

segments.speaker: goldilocks
segments.text: "Oh dear, oh dear!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Upstairs she found three beds. The great big bed was too high at the head. The middle-sized bed was too high at the foot. But the wee little bed was just right, and Goldilocks curled up and fell fast asleep.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Soon the three bears came home for their breakfast.

segments.speaker: papa-bear
segments.text: "SOMEBODY HAS BEEN EATING MY PORRIDGE!"

segments.speaker: mama-bear
segments.text: "Somebody has been eating my porridge!"

segments.speaker: baby-bear
segments.text: "Somebody has been eating my porridge — and they ate it ALL up!"

segments.speaker: papa-bear
segments.text: "SOMEBODY HAS BEEN SITTING IN MY CHAIR!"

segments.speaker: mama-bear
segments.text: "Somebody has been sitting in my chair!"

segments.speaker: baby-bear
segments.text: "Somebody has been sitting in my chair — and they broke it all to pieces!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Up the stairs they crept.

segments.speaker: papa-bear
segments.text: "SOMEBODY HAS BEEN LYING IN MY BED!"

segments.speaker: mama-bear
segments.text: "Somebody has been lying in my bed!"

segments.speaker: baby-bear
segments.text: "Somebody has been lying in my bed — and here she is!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At the sound of Baby Bear's wee little voice, Goldilocks woke with a start. She saw the three bears, tumbled out of bed, ran down the stairs and out the door, and never stopped running until she was home. And she never, ever wandered into a stranger's house again — though the three bears did fix the wee little chair, just in case a politer visitor ever came to call.
